authoredNote: Source written first from the #861 pre-declared contract (the M59 rule: the line belongs to the name). The numbers below were then read off the post-fix run; they are quoted here because they are exactly what the fixture's own text says (`@sealed` 38 / `export class Service` 39, `@inject("db")` 40 / `private pool` 41, `@sealed` 43 / `method()` 44).
rationale: M59 (#861). Contract 1 — a decorated declaration's node starts at its DECORATOR in this grammar (measured: export_statement [decorator@38, export@39, class_declaration@39]; public_field_definition [decorator@40, accessibility_modifier@41, ...]), so the symbol range and every edge derived from it named a line that contains `@sealed`, not the name `Service`. Fixed by skipping leading decorator children in nodeRange, the rule scala already uses (scala/declaration-lines-825). Method decorators are class_body SIBLINGS in this grammar, so `method` was already on 44 — pinned as the control that the defect is about the NODE, not about decorators. Contract 2 — a decorator is metadata on the symbol it decorates, not a call/reference by whoever lexically encloses it: `@inject("db")` used to emit `calls Service -> inject` AND `references Service -> inject` from the CLASS, beside the correct `references pool -> inject`; the family rule (JVM annotations are metadata; the python oracle documents it as PYD1) leaves only the member-scoped rows. RELABEL (2026-10-18, vocabulary extension): the decorator rows below are `decorates`, not `references` — a decorator is applied TO a declaration rather than mentioned in its body, and the owner admitted the canonical value; source/target/line/one-row-per-decorator are unchanged, and `forbid` now also refuses the old `references` spelling so a partial relabel cannot pass.
